about.note: The Town of Gorham, Coos County (2020 census 2,696), sits where Routes 2 and 16 meet in the Androscoggin Valley. It is run by a three-member Board of Selectmen with a Town Manager, and voters elect town officers and decide the budget at the annual Town Meeting in March (March 10, 2026, 7 PM, Gorham Middle/High School gym). The town posts agendas and minutes on a TownCloud page and video on Town Hall Streams, but the minutes files could not be opened for this record, so Selectmen meetings here are built from Berlin Sun, InDepthNH, NHPR and WFEA reporting and marked as news reports. The 2026 warrant and MS-737 budget form are posted as links that could not be opened, so the adopted budget is not confirmed. Water and sewer are run by an elected three-member Water & Sewer Commission. Schools are the Gorham Randolph Shelburne Cooperative School District (SAU 20). Plain-English summaries written by AI; items with needs_review=true are uncertain.

issues.title: Should Gorham police stay in the federal 287(g) immigration program?
issues.status: Town Meeting voters advised withdrawal in March; the police chief kept the agreement and the Selectmen took no action on April 27
issues.summary: Gorham's police department signed a 287(g) agreement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which lets local officers carry out some immigration enforcement tasks under ICE oversight. A petitioned article at the March 2026 Town Meeting asking the department to withdraw passed, but the vote is advisory: under the law the decision rests with the police chief.
points: March 2026 Town Meeting: the petitioned article (Article 17, per a resident's letter) recommending withdrawal passed (NHPR). No vote count was found.
WFEA reported the Board of Selectmen had recommended that the chief withdraw; no date or vote count was given.
April 14: the chief posted a memo to the Selectmen, the Town Manager and residents explaining his position.

April 27: at the Selectmen's meeting the chief said he still controls the department, officers act under 287(g) only during lawful police contact, and no arrests have been made for ICE. He wrote that withdrawing would cost $177,500, a 25% reduction of $710,000 in state funds the town received in 2025; the ACLU of New Hampshire disputed his memo. The board took no action.
NHPR reported Gorham police chose not to file for the federal stipend paid to participating departments.
A letter signed by 44 residents asked that the next police chief respect the town's vote; the town manager hires the chief.

issues.title: New town manager, and searches for a police chief and finance director
issues.status: Town Manager Joe Hemmings started in June; a new finance director was to start October 5; police chief candidates have been interviewed
issues.summary: Gorham replaced its town manager in 2026 and is replacing its police chief and finance director. The Selectmen hire the town manager; the town manager hires the police chief.
points: Feb 4: Town Manager Peter Gagnon said he would not renew his three-year contract, which expired June 12. Police Chief Jimmy Willhoite said he would retire later in the year and help find his replacement (Berlin Sun).

Sept 14: Hemmings said a new finance director (not named) would start October 5; the Berlin Sun reported the current director is leaving.

issues.title: How much time residents get to speak at Selectmen meetings
issues.status: Selectmen voted 2-1 on September 14 to allow public comment on any topic
issues.summary: Earlier in 2026, public comment at Selectmen meetings was limited to two minutes or less, at the chair's discretion, and only on agenda items. On September 14 the board voted to let residents speak on any topic, including items not on the agenda.
points: April 2026: InDepthNH described the rule as two minutes or less, at the chair's discretion, on items presented at the meeting.
Sept 14: Selectman Gargano proposed two minutes per resident for non-agenda items. Gargano and Kardell voted yes; Chair LeBlanc voted no.
Kardell said more open comment would bring more people to meetings. LeBlanc said her goal has been orderly, respectful meetings.
Gargano also raised holding work sessions, where the board discusses issues without public comment.

issues.title: Property taxes and the 2026 town budget
issues.status: 2026 budget voted at the March 10 Town Meeting; the 2026 tax rate has not been set
issues.next: Late 2026: state sets the 2026 tax rate
issues.summary: Residential property taxes were a theme of the March 2026 election, when an incumbent selectman lost after a debate about the tax burden shifting from commercial and industrial property to homes. Gorham's 2025 total tax rate was $23.45 per $1,000, down from $28.29 in 2024, while the town's total assessed value rose.
points: 2025 rate: town $9.03, local school $10.92, state education $0.96, Coos County $2.54; total $23.45 per $1,000 (state tax table).
Gorham's assessed value (without utilities) went from $316,677,455 in 2024 to $429,184,654 in 2025; total property taxes billed went from $10,796,368 to $11,759,761.

Feb 4: then Town Manager Gagnon said the proposed 2026 budget was less than a 1.7 percent increase over 2025. The town says its public budget hearing was held February 10 at the Medallion Opera House.

March 2026: at the election, Selectman Waddell said the rising residential share is tied to commercial and industrial values and urged residents to contact state legislators; he lost to Dr. Richard Kardell, 337 to 204.
For 2025, voters approved a $5.41 million operating budget (Article 20) at the March 11, 2025 Town Meeting (Berlin Sun).

issues.title: Ambulance transfers between hospitals
issues.status: Under discussion with the Fire Chief at Selectmen meetings this fall
issues.summary: Gorham Fire and EMS runs the 911 ambulance for Gorham, Randolph and Shelburne and also does non-emergency transports such as transfers between care facilities. The Selectmen met with Fire Chief Phil Cloutier on September 14 to discuss hospital transfers, and the Berlin Sun later reported the board continued the discussion.
points: Gorham EMS has two Type III advanced life support ambulances; daytime crews include at least one Paramedic or Advanced EMT and one EMT, with volunteers as needed.
Non-emergency transports, such as facility transfers or rides home after care, are booked through dispatch at (603) 466-3336.
Sept 14: the Selectmen met with the Fire Chief about hospital transfers (Berlin Sun photo caption).

issues.title: Grant-funded sidewalks on Main Street and Lancaster Road, and trail projects
issues.status: Grants in hand, per a March 2026 candidate interview; project schedule not found
issues.summary: Gorham has state highway grants for new sidewalks and grants for trails and trailheads. A selectman said in March 2026 that both carry heavy oversight and technical requirements that the town staff and board must manage.
points: About $4 million in highway grants for sidewalks on Main Street and Lancaster Road, per then Selectman Mike Waddell (March 6, 2026).
Almost half a million dollars in grants for trails and trailheads, per the same interview.
Waddell also named friction between motorized (ATV/OHRV) and non-motorized trail users as an issue. The Police Department lists a zero tolerance policy for OHRV violations.
